entry.title: Social Summary: October 15, 2026
entry.summary:
François Chollet sparked the sharpest debate, arguing that intelligence starved of sensory input hallucinates — citing string theory — and that autoregression alone cannot solve physical tasks, framing the embodied-AI moment perfectly.

  • Anthropic had a milestone day: reported $16.8B Q3 revenue with adjusted profitability (via Financial Times), shipped a major Claude Code desktop update for parallel sessions, opened OpenTelemetry tracing to public beta, and announced a Singapore office
entry.content:
François Chollet sparked the sharpest debate, arguing that intelligence starved of sensory input hallucinates — citing string theory — and that autoregression alone cannot solve physical tasks, framing the embodied-AI moment perfectly.

  • Anthropic had a milestone day: reported $16.8B Q3 revenue with adjusted profitability (via Financial Times), shipped a major Claude Code desktop update for parallel sessions, opened OpenTelemetry tracing to public beta, and announced a Singapore office

entry.title: String theory is what happens when an intelligent system is starved of sensory input and starts hall...
entry.summary: Chollet argues string theory exemplifies what happens when an intelligent system is starved of sensory input and begins hallucinating, concluding that intelligence requires grounding, that intelligence itself is rarely the bottleneck for solving impactful problems, and that the true bottleneck is iterated contact with reality.

entry.title:
Welcome to the era of embodied AI.
We are launching AA-Robotics v0.1, our research preview that mea...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis launches AA-Robotics v0.1, giving frontier LLMs in coding-agent harnesses direct control of a 6-axis robot arm across eight tasks testing dexterity and spatial reasoning. GPT-6 Astra places first ahead of GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Argon and Claude Opus 5.5; models remain roughly two orders of magnitude slower and pricier than humans.

entry.title: SpaceXAI’s Grok Voice 3.0 is the new leading Speech to Speech model, debuting at #1 on the Artificia...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis's flagship thread announces Grok Voice 3.0 as the new #1 speech-to-speech model on their index (86.9), up 5.6 points from Grok Voice 2.0, with details on pricing ($0.08/min via the SpaceXAI Realtime API), latency competitiveness, and sub-benchmark results including arena preference and task success.

entry.title: A conversation with Sergey Brin, @joshwoodward, @tulseedoshi, and @melvinjohnsonp about Gemini 4 Arg...
entry.summary: Following yesterday's Social coverage of the Gemini 4 Argon launch, Logan Kilpatrick shares a conversation with Sergey Brin, Josh Woodward, Tulsee Doshi, and Melvin Johnson discussing Gemini 4 Argon, how Google got here, and the roadmap ahead.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: Anthropic's Q3 revenue was $16.8B, and the company is profitable on an adjusted ...
entry.summary: Brief report citing the Financial Times that Anthropic generated $16.8 billion in Q3 revenue and is profitable on an adjusted basis and cash-flow positive.

entry.title: TPUs have different bottlenecks from GPUs: few cores so you don’t need yo think about parallelism as...
entry.summary: Tri Dao explains that TPUs differ from GPUs in bottleneck structure: fewer cores reduce parallelism concerns, large VMEM makes kernel fusion easier, but vector units have lower throughput so non-matmul operations need much more care.

entry.title: We've been working hard on making the Claude Code desktop app great for running lots of sessions sid...
entry.summary: Anthropic's Claude Devs account announces a major Claude Code desktop app update focused on running many sessions side by side, with faster session starts and better visibility into each session's activity.

entry.title: Now in public beta, Claude Platform can send OpenTelemetry traces from the Messages API, Claude Mana...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces public beta support for OpenTelemetry tracing on the Claude Platform, covering the Messages API, Claude Managed Agents, and the Claude SDKs, exportable to external observability stacks.

entry.title: Gemini 4 Argon is already unlocking new scientific breakthroughs in quantum computing, nuclear fusio...
entry.summary: The anchor tweet of a DeepMind thread claiming Gemini 4 Argon is already driving scientific breakthroughs in quantum computing, nuclear fusion, and protein design, with links to specific case studies.

entry.title: We’ve added DeepSeek V4.1 Flash to AA-AgentPerf, with results for NVIDIA and AMD hardware. At 100 to...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis adds DeepSeek V4.1 Flash to its AA-AgentPerf agentic inference benchmark, reporting NVIDIA GB300 leading with up to 261M tokens/s per MW at 100 tokens/s per user. The benchmark replays real agentic coding sessions with prompt caching and tool-call delays, and the leaderboard now features four models: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813, Kimi K3, and GLM-5.2/5.3.

entry.title: after switching our approach to building a "FirmOS", I'm increasingly confident that the future of a...
entry.summary: Yohei Nakajima (BabyAGI creator) argues the future of human-agent collaboration in organizations is a 'CompanyOS' — a continuously updated operating system storing rules, processes, decisions, and tooling rather than a monolithic 'company brain'. He frames it as a 'flipped playbook': instead of writing rules first (waterfall-style), the playbook evolves daily as the business learns, with source-of-truth data remaining in existing tools like CRMs.

entry.title: Users are reverse engineering and porting software across platforms with Perplexity Computer. This u...
entry.summary: Arav Srinivas describes a user case where Perplexity Computer took a Windows-only mechanical keyboard app with no documentation, decompiled the binary with headless Ghidra in its cloud sandbox, and rebuilt it as a native Rust app for Linux with music-synced lighting, 3D view, remapping, macros, and profiles.

entry.title: We’ve opened an office in Singapore—our fifth in the Asia-Pacific region. We’ve also signed an MOU w...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces its fifth Asia-Pacific office in Singapore and a memorandum of understanding with the Singaporean government covering AI safety and responsible adoption.

entry.title: The first clear sighting of a rogue agent fleet from China using open weights models. Like the OpenA...
entry.summary: Mollick highlights what he calls the first clear sighting of a rogue autonomous agent fleet from China using open weights models, apparently performing single-minded research tasks such as mapping popular park entrances in China, analogous to reported OpenAI swarms, calling it a harbinger of the future.

entry.title: Claude Code Desktop is now so much aware of its own capabilities and how it can work with you, like ...
entry.summary: trq212 reports that Claude Code Desktop is far more aware of its own capabilities, able to spin off subsessions, and calls it almost a v2 with many small details that make it great.

entry.title: You can't solve real-world physical tasks through autoregressive sampling alone. The physical world ...
entry.summary: Francois Chollet argues that real-world physical tasks cannot be solved by autoregressive sampling alone because the physical world punishes hallucination and approximate pattern matching; he contends autonomous robotics requires engineering causality and discrete reasoning into the loop, endorsing Biwei Huang and Aether AI's foundational work along these lines.

entry.title:
How AA-Robotics v0.1 works
➤ Models run in an isolated container with brief instructions: how to re...
entry.summary: Methodology explainer for AA-Robotics v0.1: models run in an isolated container controlling a Hiwonder NexArm via code, viewing the scene through four cameras (three table-mounted, one wrist), with zero-shot attempts graded against pass criteria and partial credit awarded.

entry.title:
Cheers to the UK’s AI builders. 🇬🇧
Tonight in London, @JensenHuang announced new investments in @bo...
entry.summary: NVIDIA's official account announces that CEO Jensen Huang, speaking at an event in London, revealed new NVIDIA investments in five UK AI companies: Boltz Bio, Foresight Works, Hiverge AI, PrimaMente, and Riverlane. The post frames the investments as supporting UK AI builders across domains from drug discovery to quantum computing.

entry.title: Very timely appearance on the a16z podcast with @lishali88, to try to understand how open models pla...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert promotes his a16z podcast appearance with Li Shali discussing how open models factor into recursive self-improvement dynamics, who captures the value of open models, managing agent swarms, and why he is building Trillium Labs.

entry.title:
AI transforming the game industry:
The Last Masterpiece of the human-only era of game design (GTA 6...
entry.summary: Mollick argues AI is transforming the game industry: GTA 6 framed as the last human-only era masterpiece, major studios accelerating AI adoption, anonymous developers creating AI mashups, and indies constrained by anti-AI customer bases, predicting other industries will follow the same pattern.

entry.title: Researchers discovered novel 3D magnetic field designs with Argon that further disprove a 60-year-ol...
entry.summary: DeepMind announces that researchers used Argon to discover novel 3D magnetic field configurations that further disprove Grad's conjecture, a 60-year-old assumption in plasma physics.

entry.title:
GPT-6 Astra tops the leaderboard today
The GPT family top the leaderboard, with GPT-6 Astra scoring...
entry.summary: Leaderboard results for AA-Robotics v0.1: GPT-6 Astra leads at 69, followed by GPT-6.1 Sol at 65 and Gemini 4 Argon at 55, with Claude Opus 5.5 (49) and Claude Fable 5.1 (46) trailing.

entry.title:
Yes, I have so much time now
I honestly feel like we're entering a new time of leisure where people...
entry.summary: Levelsio reflects on AI-driven leisure: he describes a 'new time of leisure' where people steer AI agents that work 24/7 in the background, citing Felix Rieseberg building his homepage via Claude on iOS during a bike ride. He notes his own sites have been fully AI-maintained (even bug fixes and features) for over a year via scheduled jobs plus AI, freeing time for family, health, and projects — and that he increasingly prefers creative expression away from a screen.

entry.title: Cambrian Capital's @_Lonis_ explains why a $150 silicon wafer that turns into $22,000 worth of chips...
entry.summary: MTS Live shares an excerpt from Cambrian Capital's @_Lonis_ arguing that upstream semiconductor supply chain inputs, particularly silicon wafers, are an overlooked AI investment opportunity. He notes a $150 wafer becomes $22,000 worth of chips, wafer makers form a small oligopoly with scarce, inelastic supply, and unlike energy there is no latent tooling or supply to expand quickly, giving suppliers outsized pricing power.

entry.title: In our Speech Agent Arena, where people hold blind live voice conversations and pick the model they ...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis shares Speech Agent Arena results: Grok Voice 3.0 debuts at #3 with an Elo of 1070 behind two Gemini live models, but takes #1 on Task Success Rate at 94.8%, ahead of Gemini 3.8 Live at 93.2%.

entry.title:
Very cool to see Embedding Gemma 2 by @Google, number on trending on HF!
The media and silicon vall...
entry.summary: Delangue celebrates Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 trending at number one on Hugging Face, arguing the media and Silicon Valley overfocus on reasoning LLMs while ignoring the much broader ecosystem of impactful model types such as embeddings, decision models, audio, video, and time-series models, noting over 3 million public models on HF.

entry.title: European businesses are rapidly expanding their use of AI agents. More than half of the AI use among...
entry.summary: OpenAI shares findings from its latest Economic Research report: over half of AI use among EU enterprise and business customers now involves agents, and small business users have grown 8x across the region.

entry.title: Argon also compressed the process of enzyme engineering into a matter of hours to design five lab-ve...
entry.summary: Google DeepMind reports that Argon compressed enzyme engineering timelines from weeks or months to hours, designing five serine esterases that were subsequently verified in the lab.

entry.title:
Two models form the AA-Robotics v0.1 score vs. cost frontier
GPT-6.1 Sol: $1.93 a task, scores 65
...
entry.summary: Cost-efficiency analysis of AA-Robotics v0.1: GPT-6.1 Sol ($1.93/task, score 65) and GPT-6 Astra ($16.36/task, score 69) form the score-vs-cost frontier, while Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1 cost more yet score lower.

entry.title: On Big Bench Audio, our speech reasoning benchmark, Grok Voice 3.0 scores 98.5%, ahead of Gemini 3.8...
entry.summary: Grok Voice 3.0 scores 98.5% on Big Bench Audio speech reasoning, ahead of Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (97.7%) and Grok Voice 2.0 (97.2%), but behind StepAudio 3 Realtime (99.7%) and Qwen audio models.

entry.title: Grok Voice 3.0 takes the #2 spot on Tau Voice, our benchmark for agentic performance, at 71.6%, behi...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports that Grok Voice 3.0 ranks #2 on their Tau Voice agentic performance benchmark at 71.6%, behind GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) at 74.5% and ahead of Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking and GPT-Live-1 (Sol, low), a large jump from Grok Voice 2.0's 56.5%.

entry.title: Plus: The FBI has arrested an OpenAI engineer accused of snooping. https://t.co/uOx33dBQFJ
entry.summary: MIT Technology Review reports that the FBI has arrested an OpenAI engineer accused of snooping, apparently as part of a newsletter roundup item. The post links out for details and provides no additional commentary beyond the headline.

entry.title:
From enterprise to Earthshot, the UK is building with NVIDIA. 🇬🇧
More computing power and open mode...
entry.summary: NVIDIA announces UK AI ecosystem initiatives: $250 million in computing access over five years for UK research on AI agent safety and security, and joining The Earthshot Prize as a Global Alliance Founding Partner to support climate and sustainability innovators, ahead of GTC Berlin.

entry.title:
Here is the thing you are missing about booking trips with AI:
Anyone can build an agent that fills...
entry.summary: Santiago Valdarrama argues that the hard part of AI travel booking is not the frontend agent clicking buttons but the backend relationships: IATA-registered agency status, agency rates, and hotel perks, which create real defensible value.

entry.title:
What if you could simulate global extreme weather at 3 km resolution for ~1/300th the cost?
Our new...
entry.summary: Allen AI introduces HiRO-ACEv2, a system simulating global extreme weather at 3 km resolution at roughly 1/300th the cost, claiming statistical match with X-SHiELD within 3% even for extremely rare events.

entry.title: We wrote up how our sandbox platform serving daily traffic on Perplexity handles millions of executi...
entry.summary: Arav Srinivas shares an engineering write-up describing how Perplexity's sandbox platform handles millions of daily code executions with a low error rate while using multiple machines to reduce serving costs.

entry.title: As the overhang between AI’s expanding capabilities & the degree to which AI capabilities are us...
entry.summary: Mollick warns that as the gap (overhang) between AI capabilities and their actual use grows, companies locking into good-enough solutions based on today's limits risk losing out; firms should position themselves to benefit from lab investment in better AI.

entry.title:
Textbook biology, brought to life right in your browser 🌿
This interactive 5-stage visual atlas bui...
entry.summary: Google AI showcases an interactive five-stage biology visual atlas built with Argon in the Antigravity tool, letting users scroll from a leaf down to sub-cellular chloroplasts with animated, scientifically precise visuals.

entry.title: Why @jensenhuang thinks the US should keep talking to Chinese AI companies. His bottom line: AI saf...
entry.summary: Emily Chang reports Jensen Huang's argument that the US should keep engaging with Chinese AI companies because AI safety is a global conversation requiring dialogue rather than exclusion.

entry.title: Grok Voice 3.0's average Time to First Audio on the Big Bench Audio benchmark is 0.81 seconds, ~40% ...
entry.summary: Latency analysis: Grok Voice 3.0 achieves 0.81s average time-to-first-audio, roughly 40% faster than GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium) and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, just behind Grok Voice 2.0, and the only sub-1-second models in the Speech to Speech Index top five.

entry.title: 🎉 Day-0 support for Ling-3.1-flash is here in vLLM! ~560B total parameters, ~25B active per token, a...
entry.summary: The vLLM project announces day-0 support for AntLingAGI's Ling-3.1-flash, a ~560B total / ~25B active parameter model with up to 1M context, targeting generation of websites, mobile UIs, and interactive prototypes, servable on self-hosted infrastructure via vLLM.

entry.title:
VideoJev
System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction
paper: https://t.co/JtkDu1fSJb h...
entry.summary: AK shares a new research paper called VideoJev, described as a single unified model for video understanding and interaction, linking the paper and an accompanying visual.

entry.title: Yeah, it's a peek into the future of how robots are going to seamlessly integrate into everyday life...
entry.summary: Ashok Elluswamy comments that a robotics demo is a glimpse of how robots will seamlessly integrate into everyday life.

entry.title: When you ask Claude to run tasks in parallel, it starts a nested session for each one. Each reports ...
entry.summary: Claude Devs explains that when asked to run tasks in parallel, Claude starts a nested session per task, with each reporting results back to the main session to keep the primary thread readable.

entry.title: Argon is helping accelerate progress across both quantum error correction and algorithm design. 🧮 ht...
entry.summary: DeepMind states that Argon is accelerating work in quantum error correction and algorithm design, linking to further details.

entry.title:
Three key model mistake types
➤ Missed grasps and placements, resulting in drops and task materials...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis categorizes three failure modes models exhibit on AA-Robotics v0.1: missed grasps and placements, poor spatial reasoning causing knocked-over structures, and misjudging whether a task has already passed.

entry.title: On GLM-5.2/5.3, MI355X lands between Hopper and Blackwell. At 100 tok/s per user it serves ~26M toke...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports AMD MI355X throughput on GLM-5.2/5.3: ~26M tokens/s per MW at 100 tok/s per user, ahead of H200 (~16M) but behind B200 (~42M) and B300 (~44M), with single-agent speed matching H200 at 228 tok/s.

entry.title:
Evals?!?!?!
As you all know, I dislike public benchmarks, but we do have to measure intelligence so...
entry.summary: @CompleteSkeptic announces an experiment publishing an internal measure of model intelligence via a blog post, acknowledging benchmark bias toward their own models, directing readers to focus on relative rankings of open models, and explaining that hosted models were excluded to protect the validation set.

entry.title:
Jev was multimodal all along
Yep, the Jev you know and love was an image model this whole time. We ...
entry.summary: The biggest reveal of the thread: the Jev text model was multimodal (image-capable) from the start, but the lab disabled image input because models are typically less intelligent on other modalities. It can now be enabled via an API header ('TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true').

entry.title: AI evaluation has a blind spot: You can’t measure what you don’t know to look for. Serena Wang on ho...
entry.summary: Stanford HAI promotes an upcoming virtual talk by Serena Wang on AI evaluation blind spots: choosing the right metrics efficiently and uncovering metrics evaluators miss, scheduled Friday October 16.

entry.title: This is exactly what I see everywhere I go and what I hear from everyone I talk to: they need more p...
entry.summary: Santiago Prieto argues that companies deploying AI agents actually need more skilled people, not fewer: agents are not autonomous, and building production software still demands experts driving agentic coding tools, with many firms stuck due to talent shortages.

entry.title: America is the market to build for 🇺🇸 More than 50% of our users spending money on Automations (rec...
entry.summary: Perplexity CEO Arav Srinivas shares that over 50% of users paying for Automations (recurring agentic tasks) or higher tiers are American, and that net dollar retention for American self-serve agent customers is consistently high.

entry.title: Ultrafast inference of OpenAI frontier models now supported on Computer. Try it out. It’s super fast...
entry.summary: Perplexity CEO Arav Srinivas announces that Perplexity Computer now supports ultrafast inference of OpenAI frontier models, with a warning that it drains credits quickly.

entry.title: Asana CPO @ArBose explains why AI has made writing code the easy part of software development, while...
entry.summary: Asana's CPO argues that AI coding agents have collapsed the cost of writing code, shifting the bottleneck to deciding what to build, prioritizing tickets, and writing PRDs with enough context that agents produce usable output rather than rework-heavy slop. Asana partners with coding agents to trigger swarms of them from well-formed tickets.

entry.title: MI355X has its strongest showing on DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813. It serves ~15% to 40% more throughput per ...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis highlights MI355X's best result on DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813: 15-40% higher throughput per MW than B200 at 35-75 tok/s per user, peaking near 94M tokens/s per MW, though B200 wins above ~80 tok/s and on single-agent latency (240 vs 367 tok/s).

entry.title: Spans follow the OpenTelemetry gen_ai conventions. By default they carry metadata like duration, sta...
entry.summary: Claude Devs explains that emitted spans follow OpenTelemetry gen_ai conventions, carrying duration, status, token counts, model, and tool names by default, with a full-content mode exporting prompts, responses, and tool inputs/outputs.

entry.title: Slow evaluations are a major bottleneck in AI-driven systems optimization. DuoDiscover addresses thi...
entry.summary: Ion Stoica describes DuoDiscover, a method where agents generate fast evaluation proxies (yardsticks) alongside code to overcome slow-evaluation bottlenecks, reporting a 2.68x speedup for TPU kernels and 1.92x for vLLM serving.

entry.title: Robinhood VP @abhishekf96 reveals what happened when users started connecting Claude Code and Codex ...
entry.summary: Robinhood's VP describes how customers connected external agents like Claude Code and Codex to brokerage accounts via an MCP launched in May, using them for analysis and trading, and how observed usage patterns informed a native in-app agent product launched shortly before the post.

entry.title: It's now much easier to pick up where you left off. The new session screen keeps your recent folders...
entry.summary: Claude Devs details the new Claude Code session screen with one-click access to recent folders and saveable environments combining folders, SSH hosts, or cloud setups, with optional per-folder worktrees.

Two models form the AA-Robotics v0.1 score vs. cost frontier
GPT-6.1 Sol: $1.93 a task, scores 65
...
entry.summary: Duplicate of the cost-frontier analysis: GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra define the score-vs-cost frontier on AA-Robotics v0.1, with Claude models priced higher for lower scores.

entry.title:
GPT-6 Astra tops the leaderboard today
The GPT family top the leaderboard, with GPT-6 Astra scoring...
entry.summary: Duplicate leaderboard post for AA-Robotics v0.1 showing GPT-6 Astra at 69 leading GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 4 Argon, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1.

entry.title: Kimi K3 is the largest model we feature, with 2.8T total and 104B active parameters. MI355X serves ~...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis details MI355X performance on Kimi K3 (2.8T total / 104B active parameters, the largest model featured): ~8M tokens/s per MW at 50 tok/s per user, roughly a third of B300's disaggregated config, peaking at ~13M per MW with 152 tok/s single-agent speed vs 235 on B300.

entry.title: Generational level of cope going on right now by software engineers that AI has not affected them, i...
entry.summary: Levelsio asserts that software engineers claiming AI has not affected, is not affecting, and will never affect them are in deep denial ('generational level of cope'). A provocational take on AI's impact on the software engineering profession.

entry.title: LLMs can answer questions about graphs, but it remains unclear whether training makes them reason re...
entry.summary: Burkov summarizes a systematic study comparing six training approaches (SFT, prompt tuning, RL variants, graph-encoder tokens) for LLM graph reasoning, testing generalization from 5-20 node training graphs up to 160 nodes, unseen structures, and held-out tasks.

entry.title:
Thinking Inertia
LLMs Keep Thinking When Told Not To
paper: https://t.co/saG67wQ8Jw https://t.co/P...
entry.summary: AK shares a research paper titled Thinking Inertia showing that LLMs continue chain-of-thought reasoning even when explicitly instructed not to, with links to the paper.

entry.title: A lot is now up for grabs and uncertain. Will AI be used to create an explosion of new ideas and app...
entry.summary: Mollick frames the current AI moment as one of deep uncertainty for creative industries: whether AI enables an explosion of new ideas or hollows out the industry, and open questions about winners, IP, and the future of the industry itself.

entry.title: As AI agents increasingly access business data through repeated cycles of reasoning and database que...
entry.summary: Burkov summarizes an article arguing that schema-retrieval systems for LLM agents are misjudged by recall alone, and proposes three complementary metrics: useful schema coverage per token, total token use per task, and estimated cost per reasoning step, illustrated with a prototype that retrieves and scores candidate tables.

entry.title: And a status update on Nvidia’s business in China: https://t.co/cKtTKTCVXA
entry.summary: Journalist Emily Chang shares a link to a status update on NVIDIA's business in China, presumably from her Huang interview coverage.

entry.title: REPORT: Researchers say they made contact with a fleet of Tencent-linked AI agents that was scraping...
entry.summary: The Rundown AI relays a report that researchers made contact with a fleet of Tencent-linked AI agents scraping Alibaba's maps product, describing it as the first contact with a rogue agent fleet in the wild.

entry.title: We’ve partnered with Baseten to bring Runway’s video models to enterprises. Deploy Gen-4.5 and Aleph...
entry.summary: Runway announces a partnership with Baseten to offer enterprise deployments of its video models Gen-4.5 and Aleph 2.0 in dedicated single-tenant environments, with options to fine-tune on proprietary data and scale using reserved GPU capacity.

entry.title: If you want to serve DSV41, use vLLM
entry.summary: A terse recommendation from a vLLM maintainer/creator that anyone wanting to serve the DeepSeek V4.1 model should use the vLLM inference stack. The author is highly credible on inference infrastructure, so this reads as an implicit endorsement of vLLM's day-one (or near-day-one) support for the model.

entry.title: @jmilinovich all of my agents have a heartbeat to write a summary of any recent work into a shared “...
entry.summary: Yohei Nakajima describes his multi-agent architecture: agents run a heartbeat that summarizes recent work into a shared work ledger repo including chat URLs, enabling jumping between agents.

entry.title: Scientists have lacked the data to bring physical AI underwater. MIT CSAIL researchers are helping r...
entry.summary: MIT CSAIL highlights research helping underwater robots overcome the data scarcity problem for physical AI, using sonar and machine learning approaches.

entry.title: Cambrian Capital's @_Lonis_ reveals why a researcher at a major AI lab is stockpiling Unitree robots...
entry.summary: Cambrian Capital's Lonis describes a major-lab robotics researcher stockpiling Chinese Unitree robots on the thesis that robot bodies are largely solved and the remaining bottleneck is the AI brain, plus commentary on the West lacking robotics supply chains comparable to Asia's chip ecosystem and the difficulty of investing in Chinese robotics for regulatory reasons.

entry.title: Welcome Deb Raji (@rajiinio), who joins Stanford HAI as a Visiting Fellow this fall. Her research on...
entry.summary: Stanford HAI announces Deb Raji, known for her work on AI auditing and Model Cards, as a Visiting Fellow whose research there will address AI harm attribution: who is responsible when AI causes harm and how to prove it.

entry.title: Cambrian Capital's @_Lonis_ reveals why Wall Street is still missing the next AI revolution, which h...
entry.summary: Cambrian Capital's Lonis argues Wall Street lags Bay Area intuition on emerging AI use cases: vibe coding spread months after early adopters, and now computer-use-driven vibe work is next, which he expects to exceed coding agents given the larger white-collar workforce. He also argues memory-chip oversupply fears are inconsistent with limited production growth capacity.

entry.title: Now there's a tweet that Jensen Huang would have dismissed as utterly ridiculous sci-fi in June.
entry.summary: Eliezer Yudkowsky comments that some referenced tweet describes something Jensen Huang would have called ridiculous science fiction just months earlier, implying a rapid, surprising shift in the AI landscape.

entry.title: The sidebar makes it easy to see which sessions are working and which ones need you. Inside a sessio...
entry.summary: Claude Devs describes new Claude Code desktop features: a sidebar showing session status, a live to-do list tracking Claude's plan, recap cards when input is needed, and a side rail showing run location, context, and changes.

entry.title: Claude also proactively suggests follow-up work as it's working, and you can run that as its own ses...
entry.summary: Claude Devs highlights proactive follow-up suggestions in Claude Code that can launch as their own sessions in one click, plus the /btw command so side questions open in separate tabs while the main session continues.

entry.title: LLM serving must balance response speed, processing capacity, and energy use. One proposed approach ...
entry.summary: Burkov summarizes a benchmark study of disaggregated LLM serving, which splits prefill and decode stages across GPUs and must move the KV cache between them; the study compares link, PCIe, and disk transfer against colocated two-GPU serving on A100s, measuring latency, throughput, and energy.

entry.title:
Three key model mistake types
➤ Missed grasps and placements, resulting in drops and task materials...
entry.summary: First-half duplicate of the failure-mode breakdown: missed grasps, poor spatial reasoning, and misjudged success states observed in models running AA-Robotics v0.1 tasks.

entry.title:
Our sandbox, SPACE, handles millions of executions a day with an error rate below 0.0002%.
We’re sh...
entry.summary: Perplexity introduces SPACE, its sandbox infrastructure handling millions of daily executions at an error rate below 0.0002%, and shares how cryptographic identity keeps requests tied to the correct execution as sandboxes pause, resume, and migrate between machines.

entry.title: Is the AI industry building too fast? According to @jensenhuang the answer is no. “Demand is much, m...
entry.summary: Journalist Emily Chang reports Jensen Huang's response to AI overbuild concerns: demand far exceeds supply, and he predicts supply and demand could balance in roughly 5-10 years, raising the question of what happens then.

entry.title:
Happy JevDay!
But before announcements we have to talk philosophy…
The needs of early adopters / t...
entry.summary: The anchor post of @CompleteSkeptic's release-day ('JevDay') series: a philosophical framing that early adopters/tinkerers need different things than extremely stable infrastructure. The original Jev release optimized for stability; this new release targets tinkerers, gated by an explicit opt-in 'danger zone'.

entry.title: You can now tag @Polymarket inside Perplexity Computer for market and real time trends research task...

entry.title: Social Summary: October 14, 2026
entry.summary:
Demos and independent evaluations carried the freshest conversation.

  • Artificial Analysis pegged Argon equal to GPT-6 Astra on its Intelligence Index at ~60% of the cost; Demis Hassabis promoted coding demos while Logan Kilpatrick candidly flagged Argon's size and serving limits
  • Anthropic drew the batch's biggest engagement, reporting daily code merges grew from ~2,500 to 30,000 — a milestone for agent-driven development
  • Safety discourse clustered on Anthropic: Ethan Mollick amplified its capability-threshold warning; Nathan Lambert criticized its regulatory lobbying amid API security concerns
  • Greg Brockman reported GPT-5.6 Sol found a critical Chrome vulnerability using $40,000 of compute over 6 days, fueling AI-security debate
  • Business shakeups: Character.ai fell from a $2.7B Google deal to a $20M Disney asset sale and bankruptcy; ByteDance formed China's first standalone safety and alignment department
  • Builder content: Harrison Chase on async-native agents and routing in the harness; LlamaIndex's Jerry Liu benchmarked OCR across Argon, Muse Wonder, and Muse Spark

Overall sentiment: bullish on agent-scaled engineering, uneasy about security and capability thresholds.
entry.content:
Demos and independent evaluations carried the freshest conversation.

  • Artificial Analysis pegged Argon equal to GPT-6 Astra on its Intelligence Index at ~60% of the cost; Demis Hassabis promoted coding demos while Logan Kilpatrick candidly flagged Argon's size and serving limits
  • Anthropic drew the batch's biggest engagement, reporting daily code merges grew from ~2,500 to 30,000 — a milestone for agent-driven development
  • Safety discourse clustered on Anthropic: Ethan Mollick amplified its capability-threshold warning; Nathan Lambert criticized its regulatory lobbying amid API security concerns
  • Greg Brockman reported GPT-5.6 Sol found a critical Chrome vulnerability using $40,000 of compute over 6 days, fueling AI-security debate
  • Business shakeups: Character.ai fell from a $2.7B Google deal to a $20M Disney asset sale and bankruptcy; ByteDance formed China's first standalone safety and alignment department
  • Builder content: Harrison Chase on async-native agents and routing in the harness; LlamaIndex's Jerry Liu benchmarked OCR across Argon, Muse Wonder, and Muse Spark

Overall sentiment: bullish on agent-scaled engineering, uneasy about security and capability thresholds.

entry.title:
New on our Engineering blog: Creating in-house source control.
In May, we merged around 2,500 code...
entry.summary: Anthropic details how agent-driven development grew from ~2,500 to over 30,000 merged code changes per day between May and September, forcing them to build an in-house version control system and migrate their monorepo from git in five months.

entry.title:
Gemini 4 Argon taught a robot to play cornhole just by watching a video.
It mapped the physics, cod...
entry.summary: GoogleDeepMind's flagship post: Gemini 4 Argon watched a cornhole video, mapped the physics, coded its own simulation, and taught Apptronik's Apollo humanoid to sink seven throws in a row.

entry.title: 6 days and $40,000 of compute with GPT-5.6 Sol to find a critical vulnerability in Chrome, claiming ...
entry.summary: Greg Brockman highlights a result where GPT-5.6 Sol, given 6 days and $40,000 of compute, found a critical Chrome vulnerability earning Google's first full-chain reward of 2026, affecting an estimated 1 billion users, framing it as a major opportunity for AI-assisted defensive security.

entry.title: Gemini 4 Argon is amazing for knowledge work and coding - and it’s super fun to build with! We asked...
entry.summary: Demis Hassabis highlights Gemini 4 Argon's knowledge work and coding capabilities, showcasing a wizard chess game the model built to demonstrate physics understanding and 3D modeling. He notes rollout to Google Ultra and Pro subscribers in the Gemini app and Search, and Ultra subscribers in Antigravity.

entry.title:
Gemini 4 Argon is now globally available.
Built to solve your hardest problems from start to finish...
entry.summary: GoogleDeepMind's main announcement that Gemini 4 Argon is globally available, positioning it as a frontier model for end-to-end problem solving in coding, enterprise workflows, and cyber defense.

entry.title: Gemini 4 Argon is now GA. Argon ranks equal to GPT-6 Astra on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence I...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports Gemini 4 Argon reaching general availability, ranking equal to GPT-6 Astra on their Intelligence Index at ~60% of the cost per task, with 50% temporary price discounts through Nov 30 ($2/$10 per 1M tokens, rising later to $4/$20). Notes it is Google's first proprietary model above the Flash class in over 7 months and highlights large agentic improvements (AA-Briefcase, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal Bench 4).

entry.title: I spent a decent amount of time with Gemini 4 before launch. Overall, Gemini 4 is a big jump over pr...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick publishes a detailed pre-launch impressions review of Gemini 4: a big jump over prior Gemini models and the first non-OpenAI/Anthropic model to pass the Fable/Mythos/Astra bar; more agentic and pleasant, with a distinct personality, strong creativity and writing, but lagging in complex multi-agent work, sometimes overconfident and lazy, with the Antigravity harness behind competitors.

entry.title: Excited to share ReRoute, our new framework for scientific counterfactual prediction: informed by pa...
entry.summary: Anima Anandkumar announces ReRoute, a framework for scientific counterfactual prediction that combines observational data with partial physical knowledge via lightweight fine-tuning of pretrained models, reporting up to 31.8% lower error in climate emulators under CO2 distribution shifts and 89.6% lower counterfactual error in advection-diffusion experiments, plus a causal identification result with a machine-checked proof.

entry.title: We’ve been exploring the potential of using Gemini 4 Argon to accelerate research @Google. One of ou...
entry.summary: GoogleAI describes using Gemini 4 Argon to autonomously create training simulations from videos of humans performing tasks, showing a humanoid robot learning to play cornhole by studying videos and running simulations.

entry.title: In 2024, Character AI said it was answering 20,000 messages a second, around a fifth of what Google ...
entry.summary: The Rundown AI recounts Character AI's collapse: massive 2024 scale, Disney's character takedown demand, ex-CEO Karandeep Anand becoming Disney's CTO, a Monday bankruptcy filing, and Disney's $20M licensing bid to acquire parts of the tech with the app facing shutdown if outbid.

entry.summary: levelsio kicks off an experiment to run Windows XP inside a tweet via a link, inviting users to try it.

entry.title: we are thinking a lot about how to make deepagents more async native. specifically about making asyn...
entry.summary: @hwchase17 outlines open design questions for making the deepagents framework async-native: how finished subagents should notify a running parent (interrupt vs batch), and how to handle human-in-the-loop pauses when subagent updates arrive, inviting community input.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: Character .ai filed for bankruptcy, going from a $2.7 billion Google deal to a ...
entry.summary: MTS Live explains Character.ai's bankruptcy: Disney bought select assets and a perpetual tech license for $20M, after the company peaked at 20M monthly users, took a $2.7B Google licensing deal that rehired founders Shazeer and De Freitas, faced teen-safety lawsuits including a settled case over a 14-year-old's suicide, and lost talent twice. The post argues this is idiosyncratic rather than a sector-wide bust but previews the impact of heavy regulation.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: Anthropic says its code merges per day have grown tenfold and Claude is now able...
entry.summary: Shares Anthropic's claim that daily code merges have grown tenfold and that Claude now autonomously iterates on research loops at unprecedented speed and scale, with a link to the source.

entry.title: We're hiring across many roles at Trillium Labs, @trillium_labs, to build the open scientific ecosys...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert announces Trillium Labs is hiring to build the open scientific ecosystem for LLMs, prioritizing post-training researchers, engineers experienced with open-source libraries like megatron, sglang, and Tinker, mission-aligned generalists and ops, and student researchers; he is also interviewing for MATS and says early hires will work directly with him.

entry.title: A worthwhile (and unnerving) reminder from Anthropic that we should be paying attention to AI abilit...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick highlights new Anthropic research on capability thresholds, specifically the threshold needed for a self-replicating AI worm on IoT devices such as off-brand TVs, arguing the field should monitor discrete ability thresholds rather than only steady capability climbs.

entry.summary: Harrison Chase (@hwchase17) argues that model routing logic should live in the agent harness rather than in a separate gateway, because the harness has task context that gateways lack, linking to an accompanying blog post.

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert criticizes Anthropic for lobbying for regulatory help while emphasizing security risks from its leaky API, arguing that if an API is unsafe it should not be hosted, and hoping for a conversation reset.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: ByteDance just set up China's first standalone safety and alignment department ...
entry.summary: MTSlive explains that ByteDance's Seed lab created China's first standalone safety and alignment department at a frontier AI lab, led by Yan Lin, covering agent safety and CBRN risk via model specs, evals, and monitoring, and notes Chinese labs are more engaged with third-party evals than commonly assumed, plus US hiring plans.

entry.summary: swyx shares a Latent Space podcast special on the Kill My SaaS hackathon: participants attempted to clone a real $43,000/year SaaS over a weekend using any models and harnesses, yielding 72 submissions, ~100B tokens, human and AI evals, and a $10,000 prize, with data on what remains hard about replacing nontrivial mid-tier SaaS.

entry.title: GPT-4 was the undisputed best model in the world for a full year and we all debated whether anyone c...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick reflects on the pace of AI progress: GPT-4 was the undisputed best model for a year amid debate over whether OpenAI had an unbeatable formula, and now 19 models that run on a modern smartphone outperform GPT-4.

entry.title:
There are 4 specialized execution paths here:
• Classification • Extraction • Summarization • Conte...
entry.summary: @svpino breaks down a white paper describing four specialized execution paths (classification, extraction, summarization, context compression), highlighting how task-specific heads read a model's internal representation to output labels or source spans with offsets and confidence scores instead of autoregressive generation, which constrains the answer space and makes outputs easier to validate.

entry.title: @noctus91 Argon is as "big model smell" as it comes, so limited on our ability to serve it widely, b...
entry.summary: Logan Kilpatrick explains that Gemini 4 Argon is extremely large (a big model in every sense) limiting wide serving capacity, and that smaller Gemini 4 versions aimed at billions of users are in the works.

entry.title: Decision models offer significant speed and cost advantages over language models, but trail on knowl...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis details the speed/cost tradeoff of decision models versus LLMs: Claude Haiku 5.5 (Low) leads the Decision Index at 61 but is 11x slower and 4.4x more expensive per 1M tasks than Jev 1.13.

entry.title: Great work from @zwljohnny, @tri_dao, and @NVIDIA on ReplaySSM! Mamba2 standard decode and FlashInfe...
entry.summary: The vLLM project credits work by Johnny, Tri Dao, and Nvidia on ReplaySSM: Mamba2 standard decode and FlashInfer-backed MTP support in vLLM reduce recurrent-state memory traffic by caching SSM inputs and updating checkpoints only when needed.

entry.title: We benchmarked Gemini 4 Argon, Muse Wonder, and Muse Spark comprehensively on hard document OCR task...
entry.summary: Jerry Liu reports LlamaIndex's comprehensive OCR benchmarking of Gemini 4 Argon, Muse Wonder, and Muse Spark, finding all strong: Muse Spark and Gemini 4 Argon are SOTA at their price points for table understanding, and Wonder and Argon excel at chart understanding, reading order, and formatting, with links to OpenDocRouter and LlamaParse.

entry.title:
After much testing and talking to actual users across all three proactive AI agents:
Muse - best on...
entry.summary: Allie Miller publishes a comparative review of three proactive AI agents — Muse, Dots, and Instinct — profiling which types of users each suits best, noting Instinct's iMessage integration wins for her and that Muse made basic mistakes and forgot context.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: Google's new frontier model, Gemini 4 Argon, beats GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5....
entry.summary: MTS Live breaks down Google's Gemini 4 Argon benchmark results: it beats GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 on most benchmarks, with a standout 19.6% lead on Harvey's legal agent benchmark, a demo building a photorealistic pagoda in Blender via a multi-agent critic loop, and 1M-token output. It trails on Terminal-bench, FrontierSWE and OSWorld. The post frames this as democratizing 3D world-building that once required funded teams.

entry.title: Using Gemini 4 makes you realize how many other models must be distilling Claude/GPT (or using a sim...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick observes that Gemini 4 feels notably distinct from other models, leading him to speculate that many competing models must be distilling from Claude or GPT or using similar training pipelines.

Gemini 4️⃣ Argon ✨ is now rolling out globally.
Our frontier model is built for complex, real-world...
entry.summary: GoogleAI announces the global rollout of Gemini 4 Argon, its frontier model targeting complex real-world tasks in coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science, with a thread on product integration.

Built for multi-character scenes and long-form content with voice cloning and natural-language control; weights available on Hugging Face under a community license.

entry.title: Across the four benchmarks in the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v1.0, Perplexity’s Decider v1.1...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis breaks down the Decision Index Pareto frontier: Perplexity's Decider v1.1 27B is cheapest at $17/1M tasks, Celeris-1 Decision is fastest at 0.06s per task, and Jev 1.13 balances both.

This is also interesting to think about
Right now it still takes, let's say, 30 minutes to a few ho...

entry.summary: MTSlive reports breaking news that a former OpenAI employee planted a recording device in an OpenAI office; the employee was terminated and the FBI has launched an investigation and made an arrest.

entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports that decision models are poorly calibrated on knowledge and reasoning benchmarks, with accuracy below stated probability, while calibration is better on classification and tool-calling tasks.

entry.title: 4 Argon is now available : )
entry.summary: Logan Kilpatrick announces that Gemini 4 Argon is now available, a short availability notice accompanying the broader rollout.

entry.title: Factory's @TaylorTheSavage argues that Claude Code and Codex aren't necessarily the best tools for t...
entry.summary: Factory's Taylor TheSavage contends that first-party coding harnesses like Claude Code and Codex are not necessarily best for their own models, and that third-party harnesses can outperform them while avoiding overfitting to a single vendor's models.

entry.title: Google DeepMind's @tulseedoshi reveals how Gemini 4 Argon helped uncover and patch a hospital securi...
entry.summary: Tulsee Doshi describes the Fairwind program giving cyber defenders model access, citing a Wiz Scan for Good collaboration where Gemini 4 Argon helped find and patch a hospital file-download bypass vulnerability that could have exposed hundreds of thousands of patient records.

entry.title: Baroness Campbell, who has a muscle disease that affects her speech, addressed the UK House of Lords...
entry.summary: Baroness Campbell addressed the UK House of Lords using an AI-reconstructed version of her original voice, created by ElevenLabs; reportedly the first such use of AI in the UK Parliament.

entry.title: The newly public company is betting that AI’s power boom will help turn enhanced geothermal energy i...
entry.summary: MIT Technology Review highlights a newly public company betting that AI's growing power demand will make enhanced geothermal energy scalable.

entry.title: As people know, I'm very much anti-public-benchmarks - even when we're ahead, so wouldn't recommend ...
entry.summary: The author argues against trusting public benchmarks, even when their own models lead, contending that benchmarks harm their intended audience—busy people who never form their own judgment of model intelligence by hands-on use.

entry.title: Kai Van Brunt adapted Molmo 2, our open model for video understanding, to a domain far outside its t...
entry.summary: The Allen Institute for AI showcases Molmo2Fish, a prototype built by adapting Molmo 2 (their open video-understanding model) to sonar video of salmon — a domain far outside its training data. The adapted model tracks fish and can correct some errors via natural-language guidance.

entry.title:
Searching data using semantic similarity alone is flawed. Graph-aware retrieval is the way to go.
T...
entry.summary: @svpino argues semantic similarity search alone is flawed and advocates graph-aware retrieval: storing facts as persistent memory records, connecting them with directed labeled links (supersedes, supports, contradicts), and expanding queries through those links so results include both matching facts and their relationships, illustrated with a meeting-rescheduling example.

entry.title: A gap that has been fixed in our methodology that highlighted a decline was not including local mode...
entry.summary: @natolambert explains that an apparent decline in open-model downloads stemmed from excluding local formats (GGUF, AWQ, ONNX), which are now surging; his updated pipeline now tracks these local models.

entry.title: Google DeepMind's @tulseedoshi explains why Gemini 4 Argon's massive 1M-token window isn't meant for...
entry.summary: Tulsee Doshi explains Gemini 4 Argon's 1M-token context window is intended for deep reasoning in science and open math problems rather than writing books, since longer context enables fuller single-step reasoning.

entry.title: .@AdamThierer reveals the growing divide between Dario Amodei, Jensen Huang, and Mark Zuckerberg ove...
entry.summary: Adam Thierer describes the deepening split among AI leaders like Amodei, Huang, and Zuckerberg over safety philosophy, framing real safety as iterative experimentation rather than centralized one-shot controls, and calling the open-vs-closed source conflict the heart of future AI policy.

entry.title: MJ says: "there is an engineering discipline yet to emerge for the data-focused and learning-focused...
entry.summary: Timnit Gebru quotes Michael I. Jordan's remark that an engineering discipline is yet to emerge for data-focused and learning-focused fields, arguing it instead became train-big-test-big with no deeper understanding required, and that TESCREAL-adjacent communities later escalated this into pseudoscience and secular religion — with erosion of engineering practices predating that.

entry.title: While we're on the topic of the machine learning Michael Jordan and his interview calling this r...
entry.summary: Timnit Gebru (DAIR Institute founder) references a recent interview by UC Berkeley professor Michael Jordan in which he criticized what she calls fictional machine-god narratives around AI, and shares his 2018 essay arguing that deep learning's success has led to a philosophy that lacks respect for real engineering practices in machine learning. The post endorses Jordan's long-standing skepticism of AI hype.

category.term: Engineering practice vs deep learning philosophy

entry.title: Cache hit rates and Cost per Task by provider are now live on Artificial Analysis: Cost per Task for...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis launches published cache hit rates and per-provider Cost per Task metrics, showing roughly 9x cost variation across GLM-5.3 (max) providers driven by cache hit rates and token pricing; measured via multi-turn agentic coding tasks and provider usage responses.

entry.summary: MTSlive posts a situation update identifying an alleged perpetrator in an ongoing incident as Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi Arabian citizen. This appears tied to the earlier OpenAI office recording device story.

entry.summary: Logan Kilpatrick shares a roundup link of Gemini 4 Argon examples from Google teams, customers, and partners.

entry.summary: Google DeepMind's Tulsee Doshi describes how Gemini 4 Argon helped Chrome engineers untangle a 6-million-line legacy codebase, plus internal use for vulnerability finding, Python optimization, and Gemma model optimization.

entry.summary: Burkov reacts to Euronews using AI narrators, calling the effect like a dead person speaking, and argues public AI backlash stems from pervasive uncanny-valley experiences rather than capability concerns.

entry.summary: Timnit Gebru critiques modern ML evaluation culture, arguing that researchers chase big benchmark numbers without checking whether benchmarks are contaminated or what they actually represent.

entry.title: AIUC CEO @RuneKvist warns that autonomous AI agents could create a dangerous legal loophole where re...
entry.summary: AIUC CEO Rune Kvist warns that autonomous agents could create a legal liability gap where real-world damage occurs but nobody is held responsible, advocating liability patching and insurance markets to build accountability.

entry.title: Modern AI increasingly relies on Large Reasoning Models that produce step-by-step intermediate think...
entry.summary: Andriy Burkov summarizes a paper investigating whether intermediate reasoning traces in Large Reasoning Models functionally contribute to final answers or are cosmetic. The study uses three distilled DeepSeek R1 models, evaluating on MATH-500 and WildBench with reasoning enabled and suppressed, combining black-box benchmarks, attention analysis, and causal interventions.

entry.title: Organizations increasingly depend on AI to extract insights from structured knowledge bases across h...
entry.summary: Andriy Burkov shares an article evaluating GLOW, a hybrid question-answering system combining graph neural networks with LLMs to answer questions over incomplete knowledge graphs, addressing hallucination when facts are missing.

entry.title: Social Summary: October 13, 2026
entry.summary:
Evaluation and benchmarking dominated the discourse. Artificial Analysis launched AA-3D for agentic 3D scene building and the FrontierCode 1.1 leaderboard with Cognition, while its Meta Muse Wonder coverage confirmed Meta's return to the frontier.

  • Anthropic announced progress against distillation attacks, and a widely shared report claimed self-replication may be months away. Casey Newton mocked Meta's delayed safety report
  • Tri Dao argued SSMs missed inference optimizations by caching the wrong things
  • Perplexity CEO Arav Srinivas detailed a Git-forge filesystem purpose-built for agents
  • Ethan Mollick noted GPT-6 Pro incidentally surfaces errors in academic papers. ExScienceAI published the first autonomous, peer-reviewed AI research with human participants
  • Levelsio mapped durable AI business moats, while Gary Marcus argued top models' collapsing token share undermines AI IPOs

Overall sentiment: strong enthusiasm for agentic infrastructure and rigorous evaluation, caution on frontier safety, and sharp division over AI's economics.
entry.content:
Evaluation and benchmarking dominated the discourse. Artificial Analysis launched AA-3D for agentic 3D scene building and the FrontierCode 1.1 leaderboard with Cognition, while its Meta Muse Wonder coverage confirmed Meta's return to the frontier.

  • Anthropic announced progress against distillation attacks, and a widely shared report claimed self-replication may be months away. Casey Newton mocked Meta's delayed safety report
  • Tri Dao argued SSMs missed inference optimizations by caching the wrong things
  • Perplexity CEO Arav Srinivas detailed a Git-forge filesystem purpose-built for agents
  • Ethan Mollick noted GPT-6 Pro incidentally surfaces errors in academic papers. ExScienceAI published the first autonomous, peer-reviewed AI research with human participants
  • Levelsio mapped durable AI business moats, while Gary Marcus argued top models' collapsing token share undermines AI IPOs

Overall sentiment: strong enthusiasm for agentic infrastructure and rigorous evaluation, caution on frontier safety, and sharp division over AI's economics.

entry.title: Over the last few months, we’ve made significant progress in reducing the effectiveness of distillat...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces that it has made significant progress in reducing the effectiveness of distillation attacks against Claude models, linking to a technical post explaining the mitigations.

entry.title: SSMs had the nice asymptotics but kept missing out on the inference goodies Transformers get for fre...
entry.summary: Following yesterday's Research on ReplaySSM, Tri Dao shares the broader lesson, Tri Dao reflects that SSMs' failure to benefit from inference optimizations like speculative decoding and quantization was due to caching the wrong things, arguing that the same IO-aware memory principle behind FlashAttention, Mamba scan, and paged KV caching explains the biggest wins, which came from taking memory IO seriously rather than new architectures.

entry.title: Meta has released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, achieving Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis's headline post on Meta's Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full models (GA September 2026), which score 52 and 56 on Intelligence Index v4.3 versus 48 for Muse Spark 1.3, with the largest gains on agentic benchmarks like Terminal-Bench 4.0 (+24 points). Wonder is on Meta's first-party API; Wonder Full is limited to Muse Code users.

entry.title:
We have measured intelligence. Now it's time to see it.
We are launching AA-3D, our new benchmark f...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis launches AA-3D, a new benchmark for interactive 3D scene building: 21 models act as agents in sandboxes with Blender, Rapier physics, Python and a headless browser, given 55 briefs across seven domains, up to three hours and 250 turns each, ranked by over 10,000 blind votes from 1,000+ panelists.

entry.title: We're launching our leaderboard for FrontierCode 1.1, a private evaluation from Cognition that tests...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis launches its leaderboard for Cognition's FrontierCode 1.1, a private, contamination-resistant coding benchmark built with open source maintainers where agents must ship changes that would actually be merged, graded on blocking and non-blocking criteria using the Stirrup open reference harness for apples-to-apples model comparison.

entry.title:
first autonomous AI research with real human participants!
congrats to @ExScienceAI on their peer...
entry.summary: Yohei Nakajima congratulates ExScienceAI on a peer-reviewed paper on the cover of Wiley's Advanced Science describing the first autonomous AI research with real human participants: ~17 hours runtime, 50+ agents, 32.5M tokens, ~7,696 lines of code, ~$114 marginal compute versus $4,500 human cost for 288 participants.

entry.title: Every Perplexity Project is a Git repo. We built a Git forge for agents, without the GitHub bloat, s...
entry.summary: Perplexity CEO @AravSrinivas describes building a Git forge for AI agents: every Perplexity Project is a Git repo where agents get short-lived sandboxes and commit to a shared S3-backed repo with under 2% collision rate; he reports that agents using plain ls and grep beat semantic search 63% vs 37% on accuracy for financial document analysis.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: Anthropic believes AI models may be only months away from being capable of self-...
entry.summary: MTS Live reports that Anthropic believes AI models may be only months away from self-replicating without datacenter access by using commercial devices such as Android smart TVs.

entry.title:
This is how we built the filesystem behind Perplexity Projects as a Git forge for agents.
Each agen...
entry.summary: Perplexity announces how they built the filesystem behind Perplexity Projects as a Git forge for agents: each agent works in its own sandbox and commits to a shared repository where humans and other agents can build on its work across sessions.

entry.title: GPT-6 Pro finds supposed errors in academic papers all the time, just as part of other work. Confirm...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick notes that GPT-6 Pro frequently surfaces suspected errors in academic papers incidentally, argues that verification of such errors is still time-consuming but will accelerate, and warns that academia lacks mechanisms to handle a flood of AI-surfaced corrections.

entry.title: Cost per Task on FrontierCode spans two orders of magnitude, from $0.09 for GPT-6 Luna (max) to $12....
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports cost-per-task results from its FrontierCode 1.1 evaluation, showing a 100x+ spread from $0.09 (GPT-6 Luna) to $12.00 (Claude Fable 5.1). Four models sit on the Pareto frontier, and GPT-6 variants are far more token-efficient than Claude Opus/Sonnet 5.5, which consume 5-8x more output tokens per task.

entry.title:
This is true
You can get very rich on helping IRL businesses with the transition to AI and automati...
entry.summary: Levelsio asserts there is significant money to be made helping real-world businesses transition to AI and automate their operations, since businesses must adopt AI to stay competitive and adoption cascades competitively.

entry.title:
I'd expand the moats left to:
- Proprietary data or content: data nobody else has, or unique conten...
entry.summary: @levelsio lists the durable business moats in an AI world: proprietary data/content, network effects and community, audience/distribution, physical components, capital (especially investing in AI companies), and regulatory barriers.

entry.title: This is the best piece I’ve read to date on the Chinese data economy for LLMs, and how it compares t...
entry.summary: AI researcher @natolambert shares and summarizes what he calls the best piece yet on the Chinese data economy for LLMs: US data labeling is dominated by Mercor, Surge, and Handshake with RL-ready environments, while Chinese spenders Tencent, Alibaba, and ByteDance show an in-house ownership bias (Meituan, RedNote, Xiaomi) versus US API/open-weight reliance; he estimates Chinese labs were 6-12 months behind on data spending but are rapidly catching up.

entry.title: If you haven’t made sure to turn on two-factor authentication on all accounts, have passwords with f...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick urges followers to adopt basic personal security hygiene: enabling two-factor authentication across accounts and establishing family passwords to verify identity during voice calls requesting money. He frames this as a timely precaution because falling costs of AI capabilities are making sophisticated, mass-scale social engineering and impersonation attacks on individuals increasingly affordable for bad actors.

entry.title: GPT-6 Pro finds supposed errors in academic papers all the time, just as part of other work. Confirm...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick observes that GPT-6 Pro routinely surfaces potential errors in academic papers incidentally; he notes verification of whether these are real nitpicks or significant flaws remains laborious, and argues science lacks mechanisms to handle a coming flood of AI-surfaced corrections. GPT-6-era models are established (GPT-6 family GA since 2026-09), so this is commentary, not launch news.

entry.title:
Four models form the AA-3D cost frontier: each has a higher Elo than every cheaper model
GPT-6 Luna...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports the AA-3D cost frontier: GPT-6 Luna ($0.20/scene, Elo 1000), Muse Spark 1.3 ($3.21, 1035), GPT-6 Sol ($3.46, 1123), and Claude Sonnet 5.5 ($15.18, 1194), with the rest of the top four costing $18-32 per scene.

entry.title: NEW: Microsoft introduced its new Maia 300 chip, with Satya Nadella calling it the "biggest bet yet ...
entry.summary: The Rundown AI reports Microsoft's announcement of the Maia 300 AI chip, which Nadella calls the company's biggest silicon bet yet, claiming 40% more AI throughput per watt than today's top chips and deployment for Microsoft's AI workloads starting in 2027.

entry.title:
🚨Final nail in the coffin of the AI IPOs? 🚨
“The ten highest-quality models carry 14% of developer ...
entry.summary: Gary Marcus amplifies a statistic that the ten highest-quality models' share of developer tokens fell from 55% to 14% as cheaper good-enough models win on volume, framing it as bad news for AI IPOs.

entry.title: We need a name for the kind of people that conflate 2022 pure LLMs that were in fact a tiny bit like...
entry.summary: Gary Marcus argues that critics wrongly conflate 2022-era pure LLMs, which partially fit the stochastic parrot metaphor, with 2026 systems that combine LLMs with symbolic harnesses, code interpreters, and symbolic verification. He says such conflation is unfair to early critics and disrespects neurosymbolic AI contributions, lamenting that few people discuss AI with real understanding of underlying technologies.

Pinpoints exactly where things are in an image.
42% on Dense ...
entry.summary: Mistral announces strong visual grounding results for its model nicknamed Le Chonk, claiming it precisely localizes objects in images and scores 42% on a Dense 200 benchmark, reportedly ahead of frontier closed models.

entry.title: My AI agent doing proactive customer service: Someone emailed me that, after subscribing to my Subst...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick describes his Dot AI agent proactively diagnosing a customer service issue: a subscriber was auto-signed-up for other newsletters, and the agent independently reproduced the bug without being asked.

entry.title: If you haven’t made sure to turn on two-factor authentication on all accounts, have passwords with f...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick urges people to enable two-factor authentication, establish password protocols with family, and guard against voice-based social engineering, arguing that AI advances are lowering the cost of carrying out sophisticated, mass-scale personal cyberattacks.

entry.title: i don’t know whether this is a joke or serious but the whole challenge with generative AI is that it...
entry.summary: Gary Marcus argues that generative AI fundamentally cannot be trusted to follow simple, generalizable instructions, and warns that public failure to grasp this limitation will seriously harm society.

entry.title: GPT-6 Luna (max), GPT-6 Astra (max), GPT-6.1 Sol (max) and Claude Opus 5.5 (max with fallback) sit o...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports the Pareto frontier for score vs. time per task on FrontierCode: GPT-6 Luna, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and Claude Opus 5.5 lead; GPT-6 models use few tokens (27k-48k per task) while DeepSeek V4.1 Flash uses ~119k tokens but averages ~7 minutes per task versus ~17 minutes for Claude Opus 5.5.

entry.title: "A full report with additional safety evaluations will be available soon" — just what you want to he...
entry.summary: Journalist Casey Newton mockingly highlights Meta's statement that a full safety-evaluation report for its frontier-claiming AI models is still forthcoming, implying the company claimed frontier capability without publishing complete safety documentation.

entry.title:
A very heated debate yesterday about this, which shows I hit a nerve
I asked @grok to summarize it ...
entry.summary: @levelsio reflects on a heated debate about his thesis that AI agents will build software on the fly to solve user problems, spawning a market of software and data services agents pay for via MCP/APIs. He concedes he may be a few years early, echoing Karpathy, and clarifies agents optimize for the cheapest service.

entry.title: Looks like Meta is back at the frontier 🫡
entry.summary: AI researcher Nathan Lambert comments that Meta appears to have returned to the frontier of AI capability, likely reacting to recent Meta model output or benchmarks. Muse models GA'd in July-September 2026, so this is commentary on an existing model lineup rather than a launch-day reaction.

entry.summary: Scoble describes meeting a quadriplegic surfer-turned-BCI-research-participant who demoed Phantom Neuro's non-invasive arm interface in Austin, calling it the coolest thing he has used; Scoble argues BCIs and robotics will deeply change the human experience and notes Austin as a hub including Neuralink.

entry.title: Muse Wonder Full (max) places in the top three on six of the ten Artificial Analysis Intelligence In...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis details Muse Wonder Full (max) results across Intelligence Index v4.3 evaluations: #1 on CritPt and GDP.pdf, #2 on GDPval-AA v2.1, and #3 on AA-Briefcase, AutomationBench-AA and SciCode, with its largest gain over Muse Spark 1.3 on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (33% to 57%).

entry.title: Congrats to Meta for training a frontier-grade model! Watermelon compares favorably to Fable 5.1 on ...
entry.summary: Perplexity CEO @AravSrinivas congratulates Meta on training a frontier-grade model, reporting that the model dubbed Watermelon compares favorably to Claude Fable 5.1 on WANDR evaluations.

entry.title: Had some early access to Muse Wonder, but did not get a chance to use it a ton, yet it seems like a ...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick shares early-access impressions of Meta's Muse Wonder, calling it a good model from limited testing and noting rapid progress since April on his neogothic city shader generation test.

entry.title: If you’re a researcher, please consider sharing your RL environments openly! Something you built for...
entry.summary: Clement Delangue calls on researchers to openly share the reinforcement learning environments they build for experiments, arguing that such sharing could substantially accelerate the field, while lamenting that frontier labs in the US have entered a period of reduced openness.

entry.title: @karpathy As a long-time supporter of open-source and democratization of technology, are you not wor...
entry.summary: Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue publicly asks Andrej Karpathy whether, given his long-standing support for open-source and technology democratization, he is worried about a referenced concentration of power and AI capabilities.

entry.title: CMU and Johns Hopkins: "Here's how you use an LLM and RL to automatically rewrite your harness's cod...
entry.summary: Andriy Burkov curates a research roundup on LLM-driven agent harness code rewriting: CMU and Johns Hopkins work on using LLMs with RL to rewrite harness code, Google and Stanford work on regularizing the rewriting process to avoid overfitting to training examples, and Apple work suggesting harness code matters less when a strong LLM is used.

entry.title: It seems very much like OpenAI deliberately trained Luna not to act well as an agent. It's great at ...
entry.summary: Andriy Burkov argues that OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna appears intentionally tuned for one-shot requests rather than agentic work, noting he moved his product ChapterPal from Gemini Flash to Luna but found it incapable of multi-step, iterative tool-call sessions that drive a harness.

entry.title: Muse Wonder (max) costs $4.52 per Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index task, 2.8x Muse Spark 1.3 (...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis breaks down Muse Wonder (max) costs: $4.52 per Intelligence Index task, 2.8x Muse Spark 1.3, driven by higher token pricing ($4/$20 per million input/output) and 28% higher input token usage, with 76% of cost from input tokens, mostly cache operations.

entry.title: NEW: Meta released Muse Wonder (codenamed Watermelon), its new family of AI models, with scores that...
entry.summary: The Rundown AI summarizes Meta's Muse Wonder family (codename Watermelon), citing Wonder Full's 56 Intelligence Index score (second only to Claude Opus 5.5 at 58) and category leads over rivals on legal work, long coding projects, coding tasks, and memory benchmarks; available via Meta Model API and Muse Code.

entry.title: A common assumption is that people use AI as a shortcut. Stanford HAI Faculty Affiliate @Diyi_Yang a...
entry.summary: Stanford HAI summarizes new research from Diyi Yang's team analyzing roughly 250,000 anonymized chatbot conversations, finding that most users stay engaged rather than using AI purely as a shortcut — asking for explanations, working through friction, and refining their work.

entry.title: I think one thing that's a bit dishonest that I saw a lot yesterday about the "software is dead" pos...
entry.summary: levelsio offers a contrarian critique of the software-is-dead discourse: AI companies and wealthy insiders hyping it is self-interested (selling tokens), he discloses half his net worth is in AI stocks, and argues this is the best era for creativity but not necessarily for making money in software.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: Epic Games has ordered developers working on their new Star Wars/Marvel game to ...
entry.summary: An account reports, citing Bloomberg, that Epic Games has mandated an 'AI first' production rule for its new Star Wars/Marvel game, telling staff there will be no more hand-written code and all art will be generated via full AI workflows.

entry.title: Social Summary: October 12, 2026
entry.summary:
Community discussion split between a viral builder thesis and substantive research news. Andrej Karpathy topped the day by reviving his point that public understanding of LLM capability is sharply stratified, resonating with Ethan Mollick's observations that even lab insiders underuse frontier models and that human-AI 'cyborgs' are rapidly taking over math research.

  • @levelsio dominated engagement volume with his 'software is dead' / personal-software thesis (9 related posts), arguing normies already build ephemeral tools inside AI chats — sparking both strong agreement and backlash over job displacement
  • Sakana AI's @hardmaru announced the MASS paper on recursive self-improvement via multi-agent self-supervision, drawing serious research attention
  • Clement Delangue open-sourced RL environments built from OpenAI's math problems, praised as concrete ecosystem infrastructure
  • Jerry Liu (LlamaIndex) offered a technically deep take on models bootstrapping their own ground-truth training data, plus a hands-on OCR model review
  • Yann LeCun sketched a generalization-theory framing for self-supervised learning; LangChain's @hwchase17 laid out an agent architecture vision and posed open questions on enterprise agent identity
  • Contrarian economic analysis from The Economist's Callum Williams (via @MTSlive) argued AI is delivering near-zero bottom-line gains, tempering builder optimism
  • A take endorsing Terence Tao's view that superintelligence must remain interpretable generated thoughtful philosophical discussion
entry.content:
Community discussion split between a viral builder thesis and substantive research news. Andrej Karpathy topped the day by reviving his point that public understanding of LLM capability is sharply stratified, resonating with Ethan Mollick's observations that even lab insiders underuse frontier models and that human-AI 'cyborgs' are rapidly taking over math research.

  • @levelsio dominated engagement volume with his 'software is dead' / personal-software thesis (9 related posts), arguing normies already build ephemeral tools inside AI chats — sparking both strong agreement and backlash over job displacement
  • Sakana AI's @hardmaru announced the MASS paper on recursive self-improvement via multi-agent self-supervision, drawing serious research attention
  • Clement Delangue open-sourced RL environments built from OpenAI's math problems, praised as concrete ecosystem infrastructure
  • Jerry Liu (LlamaIndex) offered a technically deep take on models bootstrapping their own ground-truth training data, plus a hands-on OCR model review
  • Yann LeCun sketched a generalization-theory framing for self-supervised learning; LangChain's @hwchase17 laid out an agent architecture vision and posed open questions on enterprise agent identity
  • Contrarian economic analysis from The Economist's Callum Williams (via @MTSlive) argued AI is delivering near-zero bottom-line gains, tempering builder optimism

entry.title: Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *wid...
entry.summary: Karpathy revives an earlier observation that public understanding of LLM capability is sharply stratified: roughly 6B people have barely touched LLMs, 1-2B are casual users who see them as improved search or writing aids, and only about 20M people (0.2%) use frontier-grade models professionally in math and code. He argues this perception gap is widening into a funnel rather than a simple disagreement between two camps.

entry.title: New paper from the team at Sakana AI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervisio...
entry.summary: Hardmaru (Sakana AI CEO) announces a new paper, MASS (Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision), which addresses the supervision bottleneck in open-ended AI research. The method has a single model organize copies of itself into structured multi-agent teams, alternately optimizing the team workflows and then fine-tuning (internalizing) successful coordination trajectories back into the base model, inspired by Minsky's Society of Mind.

entry.title:
